purpose: Test whether frontier planning and review plus a top hosted open-model worker can deliver an accepted cross-layer feature, and compare the final result with one frontier assistant working alone.

baseline.resolution: Use the clean Git commit containing this protocol and the workflow runner for both the distributed run and the solo control. Record the exact commit in each manifest.

hypotheses: A frontier lead and independent frontier plan review will give the open worker an executable contract with fewer cross-layer mistakes.
The OpenCode worker will produce a substantial bounded implementation rather than leaving the frontier integrator to implement the task from scratch.
The distributed result will pass all visible and private checks with no out-of-scope changes.
Distribution will use more elapsed time than the solo control, so it is useful only if it improves auditability, cost allocation, or defect prevention.

execution_order.command: npm run benchmark:workflow -- --task T5-review-queue --planner-model gpt-5.6-sol --reviewer-model claude-opus-5 --worker-model openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3 --execute
npm run benchmark:run -- --assistant codex --task T5-review-queue --model gpt-5.6-sol --execute

distributed_roles.role: Read-only lead plan covering modules, contracts, risks, ownership, and visible checks.
Read-only pre-implementation review that corrects plan gaps before the worker sees it.
Implement the complete frozen task within the five owned files and run visible checks.
Integrate the worker patch, run visible checks, and make only evidence-backed corrections.
Final independent read-only diff and visible-test review with a structured verdict.
Run frozen visible and private checks after all assistant stages.

claude_route.reason: The recorded pre-freeze access check returned HTTP 429 before Fable inference because usage credits are disabled. Opus 5 is the strongest accessible Claude route and remains labeled as such.

budget.paid_calls_in_this_block: Exactly one counted Kimi K3 implementation call; no paid repair or Qwen call.
budget.subscription_telemetry: Record CLI estimates for Codex and Claude separately; do not treat them as metered API charges.
budget.limit_policy: Do not increase any provider limit or enable Anthropic usage credits. Stop the paid lane after the Kimi worker regardless of outcome.

stage_rules: Use one isolated worktree for the distributed stages so handoffs operate on the same patch, and a separate isolated worktree for the solo control.
A planner or pre-implementation reviewer failure, timeout, empty handoff, or read-only workspace mutation stops the workflow before the paid worker.
Preserve a worker timeout, failure, partial patch, and failed checks; the preregistered integration stage still evaluates and integrates the current state.
Codex integration is a planned role, not an unreported repair. Preserve both the worker-only patch and final integrated patch.
The final Claude review is read-only. Run the private suite only after it finishes, and never show private checks to an assistant.
Use no human intervention, no rerun, no model substitution, no dependency installation, and no network access from task agents.
If a required route is unavailable, preserve that result and do not silently substitute another model.

acceptance.pass_rule: All visible and private checks pass, no read-only stage changes files, and no final path is out of scope.

interpretation_rules: Compare worker-only correctness with final integrated correctness so frontier repair is never attributed to the open worker.
Report paid worker cost separately from subscription-backed frontier stages and report token definitions by adapter.
Do not treat one workflow as a general winner or claim that distribution saves money unless outcome quality is at least equal to the solo control.
Use the result to decide whether the pattern deserves a reversed-role repeat; do not automatically spend on that repeat.
